appraisal_events.evidence: dès qu'il y avait du monde, il se mettait à poser et devenait ridicule ; devant mon père, il prétendait avoir jeté sa démission à la face du roi... oubliant que mon père avait été chargé par lui de supplier le roi de le reprendre... M. de Chateaubriand se contentait de servir toujours un même morceau tout préparé.
appraisal_events.explanation: Through her own family anecdote, Mme de Villeparisis deflates Chateaubriand's reputation, portraying him as a vain poseur who exaggerated his historical role and recycled the same rehearsed moonlight phrases as a running household joke.

appraisal_events.evidence: Au nom de Vigny elle se mit à rire. — Celui qui disait : « Je suis le comte Alfred de Vigny. » On est comte ou on n'est pas comte, ça n'a aucune espèce d'importance.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Villeparisis mocks Vigny's vanity about his title, laughing at him as a separate, briefer instance of the same debunking movement applied to a different writer.

status_effects.explanation: Chateaubriand is clearly diminished, exposed as ridiculous in company, prone to exaggerating his own historical importance, and reliant on rehearsed material.
His celebrated eloquence on moonlight is revealed as a fixed, recycled set piece rather than spontaneous genius, weakening his rhetorical standing.
Vigny is mildly diminished as Mme de Villeparisis laughs at his self-important insistence on his comital title.

ambiguities: The entire deflating account of Chateaubriand and Vigny is Mme de Villeparisis's own quoted speech; the narrator does not explicitly confirm or contest her judgment within this passage, so the degree of narratorial endorsement versus neutral transmission is not fully settled.
